# EDID fixtures

Synthetic 128-byte EDID base blocks for `tests/test_edid.py`. They are invented
rather than captured from real hardware: the parser only needs well-formed and
malformed inputs, and generating the bytes keeps a real display's serial number
out of the repository.

`.gitattributes` marks `*.bin` as binary so line-ending normalization cannot
corrupt them — a single rewritten byte would break every checksum here.

| File | Shape | Expected parse result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `valid.bin` | Correct header, correct checksum, `0xFC` name and `0xFF` serial descriptors | `GSM`, product code `30456`, name `LG TV`, serial `205NTKM1G347` |
| `bad-checksum.bin` | `valid.bin` with byte 127 incremented | hash only — no invented fields |
| `bad-header.bin` | 128 valid-length bytes whose 8-byte header is zeroed, checksum recomputed | hash only |
| `truncated.bin` | The first 40 bytes of `valid.bin`, as a short i2c read produces | hash only |

Every case still yields a SHA-256, which is the point: a hash alone tells the
control plane that the panel on a connector changed, even when nothing
descriptive could be read.

They were generated by the script below. Re-run it only if the parser's
expectations change, and update the table above to match.

```python
HEADER = bytes((0x00, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x00))


def manufacturer_bytes(letters):
    packed = 0
    for letter in letters:
        packed = (packed << 5) | (ord(letter) - ord("A") + 1)
    return packed.to_bytes(2, "big")


def text_descriptor(tag, text):
    body = (text.encode("ascii") + b"\n").ljust(13, b" ")[:13]
    return bytes((0x00, 0x00, 0x00, tag, 0x00)) + body


def timing_descriptor():
    return bytes((0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x10, 0x00)) + bytes(13)


def build(manufacturer, product_code, serial_number):
    block = bytearray(128)
    block[0:8] = HEADER
    block[8:10] = manufacturer_bytes(manufacturer)
    block[10:12] = product_code.to_bytes(2, "little")
    block[12:16] = serial_number.to_bytes(4, "little")
    block[16] = 20                      # week of manufacture
    block[17] = 34                      # year, 1990 + 34
    block[18], block[19] = 1, 4         # EDID 1.4
    block[54:72] = timing_descriptor()
    block[72:90] = text_descriptor(0xFC, "LG TV")
    block[90:108] = text_descriptor(0xFF, "205NTKM1G347")
    block[108:126] = timing_descriptor()
    block[126] = 0                      # extension blocks
    block[127] = (-sum(block[:127])) % 256
    return block


valid = build("GSM", 30456, 12345678)
open("valid.bin", "wb").write(bytes(valid))

bad_checksum = bytearray(valid)
bad_checksum[127] = (bad_checksum[127] + 1) % 256
open("bad-checksum.bin", "wb").write(bytes(bad_checksum))

bad_header = bytearray(valid)
bad_header[0:8] = bytes(8)
bad_header[127] = (-sum(bad_header[:127])) % 256
open("bad-header.bin", "wb").write(bytes(bad_header))

open("truncated.bin", "wb").write(bytes(valid[:40]))
```
